newsitem.title: SPAIN: Catalans move toward 1997 budget deal with Madrid.
newsitem.headline: Catalans move toward 1997 budget deal with Madrid.

text.p: The Spanish government was moving closer to a deal on the 1997 budget with its Catalan allies, but nothing has been finalised, Francesc Homs, Catalan economic spokesman in parliament told Spanish radio on Thursday.

"The formula is basically to recognise the real budget - to incorporate real health spending in the 1997 budget over the 1995 and 1996 base," Homs told Spanish national radio. "The discussion is over this base."

The budget talks between the allies have been stymied by a Catalan demand for 32 billion pesetas in 1997 health funding from the central government. The government budget draft must be presented to the parliament in just over 10 days.
There was speculation the Catalans might be satisfied with less, but Homs said the talks were not over specific numbers.
"The truth is that we aren't approaching it from a specific quantity or number," Homs said.
Although there had been progress, Homs said that no deal had yet been agreed.
"There is no technical solution to resolve the problem yet (but) there is the will."
